newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to tender for 54,000T corn - trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to tender for 54,000T corn - trade.

text.p: Taiwan is expected to tender for 54,000 tonnes of corn this week after buying 114,000 tonnes last week, traders said on Monday.
Traders said concerns that corn future prices may bottom out would prompt Taiwanese buyers to start October purchases.
"Taiwan corn buyers may not want to wait much longer for their October purchases than this week," a trader said. "Buyers worry that the corn futures' bear trend may switch."

A corn buyer said the July corn futures contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) showed strong support at the US$2.50 a bushel level. The CBOT closed on Friday 3-3/4 U.S. cents up at $2.51-1/2 a bushel.
Soybean buyers, on the other hand, have completed their buying through to September and were not expected in the market, traders said.
Wheat buyers were also expected to stay sidelined since Taiwan's near-term needs have already been filled.
Freight rates from the U.S. Pacific Northwest were quoted at about $11.50 a tonne while rates from the Gulf of Mexico reached $21.00 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized July shipments.
